references.text: The Lord reveals himself to Abram and promises the land to his descendants – the same land promise that is passed on to Jacob.
God appears to Isaac and identifies himself as Abraham's God, confirming the promise of land and descendants, parallel to the promise given to Jacob.
The land promise is repeated to Jacob after his name change to Israel, as a confirmation of the same promise from Bethel.
God promises Abram all the land he can see, to him and his descendants forever – the same land promise that is passed on to Jacob.
God identifies himself to Moses as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the same self-identification found in Jacob's dream at Bethel.
Jacob recalls that God Almighty revealed himself to him in Luz (Bethel) and promised him land and descendants.
The promise of the land given to Jacob in his dream is confirmed as an oath-bound covenant during the exodus from Egypt.
The founding moment at Bethel is revisited as a historical reality just before entering Canaan.
Jacob uses the promise from Bethel (28:13) as the theological basis for his prayer by the Jabbok River.
The promise given to Jacob at Bethel is shown as fulfilled in the vision from Mount Nebo, even though Moses is not allowed to enter.
God's identity as the God of Abraham and Isaac, discovered at Bethel, becomes the foundation for Moses' authority over the people.
The personal revelation of God's name at Bethel is expanded into an eternal title for the entire nation of Israel.
God's relationship with the patriarchs, confirmed at Bethel, is used as the basis for deliverance from Egypt.
The prophet's appeal to God's oath in Ezekiel builds directly on the land promises given to Jacob's descendants at Bethel.
